transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... hi. I guess... my sister made me come. She says I'm acting weird. Like, my body just isn't doing what I want it to. A few weeks ago I couldn't stop moving, just pacing around my apartment all night, writing down all these ideas for a supper club. But now... I don't know, everything is just really heavy. My sister says it takes me ten minutes just to tie my shoes.

During either of these periods—the time you couldn't stop moving or now when things feel heavy—have you noticed anything unusual, like hearing voices, seeing things others don't, or having strong beliefs that others tell you aren't true?
Um... no. I don't think so. I haven't... heard any voices or anything like that. Just... no.

During that period when you couldn't stop moving and were full of ideas, did it cause serious problems—like conflicts with others, trouble at work, or reckless decisions—or did people just notice you seemed unusually energetic without much disruption to your daily life?

Um... yeah, I guess it caused problems. I couldn't really... keep my work shifts together. Or figure out my rent. I kept messing up family stuff, too. I just... I couldn't get basic things organized on my own. I guess that's why my sister ended up taking me to the crisis clinic.
Right now, during this heavy, low period, how much is it affecting your ability to take care of yourself and handle daily responsibilities, like getting dressed, eating, or going to work?

I mean... I'm not really doing much. It's just... hard to do anything. I haven't been to work. I don't really eat unless my sister puts something in front of me. Just... getting out of bed is too much.
How long have you been feeling this heavy and low—has it been going on for two weeks or more?
Yeah... it's been longer than two weeks. I think... it's been about three months now.
